newsitem.title: UK: Conservative Party support drops in Scotland.
newsitem.headline: Conservative Party support drops in Scotland.

text.p: Scottish support for Britain's ruling Conservatives has dropped back to half the 1992 general election level in the latest survey of voting intentions.

The monthly System Three poll published in the Herald newspaper on Tuesday found support for Prime Minister John Major's party two points down at 13 percent. Labour, the dominant party in Scotland, gained one to 49 percent.
The pro-independence Scottish National Party (SNP) slumped five to 24 while Liberal Democrats gained five to 12 percent.
Analysts said the changes reflected changing support by women voters and reaction to the annual conferences of the two parties.

The poll was held in 39 of Scotland's 72 parliamentary constituencies between September 26 and Ocotber 1. Labour leader Tony Blair has promised a separate Scottish parliament if he wins a general election, which must be held byMay next year.
Major rejects any change to the 300-year old union between England and Scotland.
At present there are 10 Scottish Conservative members of parliament. Labour has 49, Liberal Democrats 9, and SNP four.
